rationale:
bugs_open/110 candidate 2, and the change is ALREADY WRITTEN, COMMITTED (ca4071c82) and its migration APPLIED — this is a review of shipped-but-inert code, not a proposal. The Go half stays inert until the next chassis roll, so a REVISE is still actionable.

THE DEFECT. platform/aiservice/gemini.go computes four values and writes them into the options map. None has a reader outside platform/aiservice/. They reach no column and no query, so thinking cost — which BILLS AS OUTPUT, and where essentially all of Gemini's spend lives — is unanswerable from any query. page-content-writer runs once per section across the whole estate, and the owner has asked to keep an eye on the cost. 016b section 9: "a field is only as live as its LAST reader".

This is also the bug that caught an overclaim of my own workstream's: bugs_open/107, its council submission (corr a1a5cf20) and three commit messages all said this change made thinking "visible to logging". It was written and never persisted. Nobody caught it, including a ten-seat council one of whose seats discussed these very fields, because "writes the field" and "the field is readable" look identical in a diff.

TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS I WANT LOOKED AT, both deviations from the filed candidate:

(1) I DID NOT ADD THE COLUMN THE BUG FILE NAMES. 110 lists visible_budget_tokens among the four. That value is already llm_call_log.max_tokens: candidate 1 made __sent_max_tokens its sole feed precisely so the column means the caller's answer-budget for EVERY provider. Adding visible_budget_tokens would give one meaning two column names — which is the exact defect 110 exists to close, reproduced a third time. I added wire_max_output_tokens instead, the genuinely unpersisted sent-side value. The bug file's key name __sent_visible_budget_tokens does not exist in gemini.go at all; I grepped the four that DO exist and used that name as a negative control (0 hits).

(2) I DELIBERATELY BYPASSED THE PACKAGE'S OWN nullIfZero() HELPER, which every other int field in LLMCallLogParams uses. It maps 0 to NULL. For thinking_tokens that would collapse "a thinking model that spent no thinking" into "this provider has no thinking concept" — the empty-vs-absent confusion this bug is itself an instance of, and the thing migration 243's header warns about one table over. So the four params are interface{}, nil ONLY when the option key was absent. Consequence worth challenging: anthropic and ollama rows carry four NULLs forever, which I claim is honest rather than lossy.

A THIRD CHOICE I THINK IS RIGHT BUT IS NOT FORCED: I read the telemetry on the FAILURE path as well as the success path. gemini.go records usage into the options map BEFORE it inspects finishReason, so a call cut short by thinking still carries the count that explains why. A failed row with thinking_tokens close to wire_max_output_tokens is the starvation signature, readable without any arithmetic on output_tokens — and 107 was misdiagnosed as an incapable model precisely because that number was invisible.

NOT CLAIMED: that this makes cost correct or complete. It makes it measurable. No backfill is possible — the values were never persisted anywhere to backfill from, so every existing row stays NULL, and every row stays NULL until the image rolls.

plan.summary: Persist the four thinking-model telemetry values gemini.go already computes: four nullable integer columns on llm_call_log, read at both LogLLMCall sites, preserving the nil-vs-zero distinction the columns depend on.

edits.rationale: Four nullable integer columns. Nullable because NULL means 'this provider does not report it' (anthropic, ollama), which is a real distinction from a reported zero. No index: these are aggregation targets over a provider+date range, not selective predicates, and llm_call_log already carries five indexes on a high-write table.
Extractor plus four struct fields. interface{} rather than int so nil and 0 stay distinguishable; a wrong-typed value reads as absent rather than panicking inside a fire-and-forget logging goroutine.

Extend the INSERT to 26 placeholders and pass the four through WITHOUT nullIfZero(), which every neighbouring int uses. That helper maps 0 to NULL and would make a reported zero indistinguishable from an unreported one.

edits.rationale: Five tests. The key names are a contract with gemini.go that the compiler cannot check — a typo yields nil, which is indistinguishable from a provider that reports nothing, so the column would sit quietly NULL forever. Also covers the nil/0 distinction, nil options, and a wrong-typed value.

grounded_in: platform/aiservice/gemini.go:321 (comment) — "The wire total is kept below for whoever needs it, but note it is currently PERSISTED NOWHERE: llm_call_log has no column for it, and nothing outside this package reads these keys. That is 110 candidate 2 (a migration), and until it lands, thinking cost is visible only in the truncation error — not in any query."

platform/aiservice/gemini.go:326-328 — the three sent-side keys, verbatim: options["__sent_max_tokens"] = visibleBudget / options["__sent_wire_max_output_tokens"] = totalBudget / options["__sent_thinking_reserve_tokens"] = totalBudget - visibleBudget

platform/aiservice/gemini.go:410-411 — the two usage keys, verbatim: options["__usage_thinking_tokens"] = response.UsageMetadata.ThoughtsTokenCount / options["__usage_total_tokens"] = response.UsageMetadata.TotalTokenCount. Both are set inside `if options != nil` BEFORE the finishReason and RefusalError checks below, which is why the failure path can read them.
bugs_open/110 — "**Verified by grep: none has any reader outside `platform/aiservice/`.** They reach no column and no query. This is `016b` §9's *\"a field is only as live as its LAST reader\"*"

bugs_open/110 candidate 2, verbatim — "**2 — Persist what the client already computes.** Add `visible_budget_tokens`, `thinking_reserve_tokens`, `thinking_tokens`, `total_output_tokens` to `llm_call_log`; read the four `__` fields in `ai_actions.go` and pass them through `llm_call_logger.go`." I deviate on the FIRST column name only, for the reason in the rationale.

platform/orchestration/actions/llm_call_logger.go (pre-existing helper) — "// nullIfZero returns nil for zero token counts (when provider doesn't report them)". This is the helper I deliberately do NOT use for the four new fields.

Live DB, after applying 245 (information_schema.columns on llm_call_log): wire_max_output_tokens | integer | YES, thinking_reserve_tokens | integer | YES, thinking_tokens | integer | YES, total_output_tokens | integer | YES.

Live DB, the first Gemini rows ever recorded (2026-07-27 20:09, page-content-writer building dartsonline/sale): provider=gemini, model_resolved=gemini-pro-latest, max_tokens=8000 for both. max_tokens reading 8000 rather than the reserve-inflated 16192 is bugs_open/110 candidate 1's own stated post-fix test, so candidate 1 is confirmed live and this change builds on it.
plan.risks: The Go half is INERT until the next chassis image rolls, so every new column reads NULL until then; that is honest (the data genuinely was not captured) but anyone querying early will see an empty feature and may think it failed. No backfill is possible — the values were never persisted anywhere to backfill from. The four columns are NULL forever for anthropic and ollama, which is intended but means any aggregate must handle NULL rather than assuming 0. thinkingTelemetry's key names are a contract with platform/aiservice/gemini.go that the compiler cannot enforce: if a future edit renames a key there, this reads nil and the column goes quietly NULL, which looks exactly like a provider that reports nothing — the test pins the literals, which is the only guard available. Widening the INSERT from 22 to 26 placeholders touches the single write path for llm_call_log; it is fire-and-forget in a goroutine with errors logged and never blocking, so a column mismatch degrades logging rather than the workflow, but it would degrade it for EVERY provider, not just Gemini.
